sanskrit: vindānuvindau sahitau suvarmāṇaṃ ca te sutam prahasann iva kaunteyaḥ śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Vinda and Anuvinda together, and your son Suvarman as well — the son of Kuntī, as though smiling, dispatched them all with his arrows to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudarśanaṃ vīraṃ putraṃ te bharatarṣabha vivyādha samare tūrṇaṃ sa papāta mamāra ca
english: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, he swiftly pierced your heroic son Sudarśana in the battle, and that one fell and died.

sanskrit: so 'cireṇaiva kālena tad rathānīkam āśugaiḥ diśaḥ sarvāḥ samabhyasya vyadhamat pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: In but a little while the son of Pāṇḍu, scattering them with his swift shafts in every direction, shattered that division of chariots.

sanskrit: tato vai rathaghoṣeṇa garjitena mṛgā iva vadhyamānāś ca samare putrās tava viśāṃ pate prādravan sarathāḥ sarve bhīmasenabhayārditāḥ
english: Then, O lord of peoples, like deer at the thunder of his chariot's roar, your sons, slaughtered in the battle and afflicted with dread of Bhīmasena, all fled away together with their chariots.

sanskrit: anuyāya tu kaunteyaḥ putrāṇāṃ te mahad balam vivyādha samare rājan kauraveyān samantataḥ
english: But the son of Kuntī, pursuing the great host of your sons, O king, pierced the Kauravas on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā mahārāja bhīmasenena tāvakāḥ tyaktvā bhīmaṃ raṇe yānti codayanto hayottamān
english: Being slaughtered by Bhīmasena, O great king, your men abandoned Bhīma in the fight and fled, urging on their finest horses.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu nirjitya samare bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ siṃhanādaravaṃ cakre bāhuśabdaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Having vanquished them in the battle, the mighty Bhīmasena, son of Pāṇḍu, let loose a lion's roar and clapped his arms in challenge.

sanskrit: talaśabdaṃ ca sumahat kṛtvā bhīmo mahābalaḥ vyatītya rathinaś cāpi droṇānīkam upādravat
english: And making a great resounding clap of his palms, the mighty Bhīma, leaving the chariot-warriors behind, charged upon Droṇa's division.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tam uttīrṇaṃ rathānīkāt tamaso bhāskaraṃ yathā didhārayiṣur ācāryaḥ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Saṃjaya said: As he emerged from that division of chariots like the sun from darkness, the preceptor, seeking to hold him back, overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: pibann iva śaraughāṃs tān droṇacāpavarātigān so 'bhyavartata sodaryān māyayā mohayan balam
english: As though drinking up those floods of shafts loosed from the foremost bow of Droṇa, he advanced against his brothers, bewildering the host with his cunning.

sanskrit: taṃ mṛdhe vegam āsthāya paraṃ paramadhanvinaḥ coditās tava putraiś ca sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Putting forth their utmost speed in the fray, those mighty archers, urged on by your sons, surrounded him on every side.

sanskrit: sa tathā saṃvṛto bhīmaḥ prahasann iva bhārata udayacchad gadāṃ tebhyo ghorāṃ tāṃ siṃhavan nadan avāsṛjac ca vegena teṣu tān pramathad balī
english: Thus hemmed in, Bhīma, as though laughing, O Bhārata, raised against them that terrible mace and, roaring like a lion, hurled it among them with force, and the mighty one crushed them.

sanskrit: sendrāśanir ivendreṇa praviddhā saṃhatātmanā ghoṣeṇa mahatā rājan pūrayitveva medinīm jvalantī tejasā bhīmā trāsayām āsa te sutān
english: Like the thunderbolt hurled by Indra with a steadfast aim, O king, filling the earth as it were with its mighty din, blazing with splendor and terrible, it struck terror into your sons.

sanskrit: tāṃ patantīṃ mahāvegāṃ dṛṣṭvā tejobhisaṃvṛtām prādravaṃs tāvakāḥ sarve nadanto bhairavān ravān
english: Seeing that mace of tremendous speed descending, wreathed in splendor, your men all fled, uttering frightful cries.

sanskrit: taṃ ca śabdam asaṃsahyaṃ tasyāḥ saṃlakṣya māriṣa prāpatan manujās tatra rathebhyo rathinas tadā
english: And marking that unbearable sound of it, O sir, the men there, the chariot-warriors, fell down then from their chariots.

sanskrit: sa tān vidrāvya kaunteyaḥ saṃkhye 'mitrān durāsadaḥ suparṇa iva vegena pakṣirāḍ atyagāc camūm
english: Having put his foes to flight in the battle, the unassailable son of Kuntī, swift as Suparṇa the king of birds, passed beyond the host.

sanskrit: tathā taṃ viprakurvāṇaṃ rathayūthapayūthapam bhāradvājo mahārāja bhīmasenaṃ samabhyayāt
english: As Bhīmasena, that leader among the leaders of chariot-troops, was thus working havoc, the son of Bharadvāja, O great king, advanced against him.

sanskrit: droṇas tu samare bhīmaṃ vārayitvā śarormibhiḥ akarot sahasā nādaṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ bhayam ādadhat
english: But Droṇa, having checked Bhīma in the battle with waves of arrows, suddenly raised a shout, striking dread into the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tad yuddham āsīt sumahad ghoraṃ devāsuropamam droṇasya ca mahārāja bhīmasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: That fight between Droṇa and the great-souled Bhīma, O great king, was vast and terrible, like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: yadā tu viśikhais tīkṣṇair droṇacāpaviniḥsṛtaiḥ vadhyante samare vīrāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: When the warriors were being slain in the battle by hundreds and by thousands by the keen shafts loosed from Droṇa's bow,

sanskrit: tato rathād avaplutya vegam āsthāya pāṇḍavaḥ nimīlya nayane rājan padātir droṇam abhyayāt
english: then the son of Pāṇḍu, leaping down from his chariot and gathering his speed, closing his eyes, O king, advanced on foot against Droṇa.

sanskrit: yathā hi govṛṣo varṣaṃ pratigṛhṇāti līlayā tathā bhīmo naravyāghraḥ śaravarṣaṃ samagrahīt
english: Just as a bull receives the rain at his ease, so Bhīma, that tiger among men, took upon himself the shower of arrows.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare rathaṃ droṇasya māriṣa īṣāyāṃ pāṇinā gṛhya pracikṣepa mahābalaḥ
english: Though thus assailed in the battle, the mighty one, O sir, seized Droṇa's chariot by the shaft-pole with his hand and flung it away.

sanskrit: droṇas tu satvaro rājan kṣipto bhīmena saṃyuge ratham anyaṃ samāsthāya vyūhadvāram upāyayau
english: But Droṇa, hurled aside by Bhīma in the fight, O king, swiftly mounted another chariot and made his way to the gateway of the battle-array.

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe tasya yantā tūrṇam aśvān acodayat bhīmasenasya kauravya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: In that instant Bhīmasena's charioteer swiftly urged on his horses, O Kaurava, and that was a wondrous thing to behold.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āsthāya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ abhyavartata vegena tava putrasya vāhinīm
english: Then, having mounted his own chariot, the mighty Bhīmasena charged with speed against the host of your son.

sanskrit: sa mṛdnan kṣatriyān ājau vāto vṛkṣān ivoddhataḥ agacchad dārayan senāṃ sindhuvego nagān iva
english: Crushing the warriors in the fray like a raging wind that crushes trees, he went on, cleaving the army like a river's current rending its banks.

sanskrit: bhojānīkaṃ samāsādya hārdikyenābhirakṣitam pramathya bahudhā rājan bhīmasenaḥ samabhyayāt
english: Reaching the Bhoja division, guarded by the son of Hṛdika, Bhīmasena, having broken it utterly, O king, pressed onward.

sanskrit: saṃtrāsayann anīkāni talaśabdena māriṣa ajayat sarvasainyāni śārdūla iva govṛṣān
english: Terrifying the troops with the clap of his palms, O sir, he overcame all the armies as a tiger overcomes bulls.

sanskrit: bhojānīkam atikramya kāmbojānāṃ ca vāhinīm tathā mlecchagaṇāṃś cānyān bahūn yuddhaviśāradān
english: Passing beyond the Bhoja division and the host of the Kāmbojas, and likewise many other bands of barbarians skilled in warfare,

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ cāpi saṃprekṣya yudhyamānaṃ nararṣabham rathena yattaḥ kaunteyo vegena prayayau tadā
english: and beholding Sātyaki too, that bull among men, fighting, the son of Kuntī, intent in his chariot, then sped onward swiftly.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno mahārāja draṣṭukāmo dhanaṃjayam atītya samare yodhāṃs tāvakān pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Bhīmasena, O great king, the son of Pāṇḍu, longing to behold Dhanaṃjaya, passed beyond your warriors in the battle.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad arjunaṃ tatra yudhyamānaṃ nararṣabham saindhavasya vadhārthaṃ hi parākrāntaṃ parākramī
english: That valiant one beheld Arjuna there, that bull among men, fighting and striving valiantly for the slaying of the lord of the Sindhus.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvātha cukrośa mahato ravān taṃ tu tasya mahānādaṃ pārthaḥ śuśrāva nardataḥ
english: Seeing Arjuna there, he then sent forth mighty roars, and the son of Pṛthā heard that great shout of his as he roared.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahānādaṃ muñcan vai mādhavaś ca ha abhyayātāṃ mahārāja nardantau govṛṣāv iva
english: Then the son of Pṛthā, uttering a great shout, and Mādhava as well, advanced, O great king, both roaring like bulls.

sanskrit: vāsudevārjunau śrutvā ninādaṃ tasya śuṣmiṇaḥ punaḥ punaḥ praṇadatāṃ didṛkṣantau vṛkodaram
english: Vāsudeva and Arjuna, hearing the roar of that impetuous one, cried out again and again, longing to behold Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaravaṃ śrutvā phalgunasya ca dhanvinaḥ aprīyata mahārāja dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Hearing the roar of Bhīmasena and of Phalguna the archer, the son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, rejoiced, O great king.

sanskrit: viśokaś cābhavad rājā śrutvā taṃ ninadaṃ mahat dhanaṃjayasya ca raṇe jayam āśāstavān vibhuḥ
english: The king became free of sorrow on hearing that mighty roar, and the lord hoped for Dhanaṃjaya's victory in the battle.

sanskrit: tathā tu nardamāne vai bhīmasene raṇotkaṭe smitaṃ kṛtvā mahābāhur dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: As Bhīmasena thus roared, fierce in the fray, the mighty-armed son of Dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira, smiled,

sanskrit: hṛdgataṃ manasā prāha dhyātvā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ dattā bhīma tvayā saṃvit kṛtaṃ guruvacas tathā
english: and that best of the upholders of righteousness, reflecting, spoke within his heart: 'You have given the signal, Bhīma, and so have fulfilled your elder's word.'

sanskrit: na hi teṣāṃ jayo yuddhe yeṣāṃ dveṣṭāsi pāṇḍava diṣṭyā jīvati saṃgrāme savyasācī dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: 'There is no victory in war for those whose enemy you are, O son of Pāṇḍu. By good fortune, Dhanaṃjaya the ambidextrous archer yet lives in the battle.'

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca kuśalī vīraḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ diṣṭyā śṛṇomi garjantau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: 'By good fortune the hero Sātyaki, of true valor, is safe; by good fortune I hear Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya roaring.'

sanskrit: yena śakraṃ raṇe jitvā tarpito havyavāhanaḥ sa hantā dviṣatāṃ saṃkhye diṣṭyā jīvati phalgunaḥ
english: 'He by whom, after vanquishing Śakra in battle, the bearer of oblations was gratified — that slayer of foes in the fight, Phalguna, by good fortune lives.'

sanskrit: yasya bāhubalaṃ sarve vayam āśritya jīvitāḥ sa hantā ripusainyānāṃ diṣṭyā jīvati phalgunaḥ
english: 'He upon the strength of whose arms we all depend for our lives — that destroyer of enemy hosts, Phalguna, by good fortune lives.'

sanskrit: nivātakavacā yena devair api sudurjayāḥ nirjitā rathinaikena diṣṭyā pārthaḥ sa jīvati
english: 'He by whom, a single chariot-warrior, the Nivātakavacas, hard for even the gods to conquer, were overcome — by good fortune that son of Pṛthā lives.'

sanskrit: kauravān sahitān sarvān gograhārthe samāgatān yo 'jayan matsyanagare diṣṭyā pārthaḥ sa jīvati
english: 'He who vanquished all the Kauravas gathered together for the seizing of the cattle at the city of the Matsyas — by good fortune that son of Pṛthā lives.'

sanskrit: kālakeyasahasrāṇi caturdaśa mahāraṇe yo 'vadhīd bhujavīryeṇa diṣṭyā pārthaḥ sa jīvati
english: 'He who slew fourteen thousand Kālakeyas in the great battle by the might of his arms — by good fortune that son of Pṛthā lives.'

sanskrit: gandharvarājaṃ balinaṃ duryodhanakṛtena vai jitavān yo 'stravīryeṇa diṣṭyā pārthaḥ sa jīvati
english: 'He who, on account of Duryodhana's plight, vanquished by the power of his weapons the mighty king of the Gandharvas — by good fortune that son of Pṛthā lives.'

sanskrit: kirīṭamālī balavāñ śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ mama priyaś ca satataṃ diṣṭyā jīvati phalgunaḥ
english: 'The mighty one crowned with the diadem, with white steeds and Kṛṣṇa for charioteer, ever dear to me — by good fortune Phalguna lives.'

sanskrit: putraśokābhisaṃtaptaś cikīrṣuḥ karma duṣkaram jayadrathavadhānveṣī pratijñāṃ kṛtavān hi yaḥ kaccit sa saindhavaṃ saṃkhye haniṣyati dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: 'He who, burning with grief for his son and resolved to accomplish a hard deed, seeking the slaying of Jayadratha, took an oath — will that Dhanaṃjaya, I wonder, slay the lord of the Sindhus in battle?'

sanskrit: kaccit tīrṇapratijñaṃ hi vāsudevena rakṣitam anastamita āditye sameṣyāmy aham arjunam
english: 'Shall I, I wonder, meet Arjuna before the sun has set — Arjuna with his vow fulfilled, guarded by Vāsudeva?'

sanskrit: kaccit saindhavako rājā duryodhanahite rataḥ nandayiṣyaty amitrāṇi phalgunena nipātitaḥ
english: 'Shall the king of the Sindhus, who delights in Duryodhana's welfare, struck down by Phalguna, gladden our foes — or not?'

sanskrit: kaccid duryodhano rājā phalgunena nipātitam dṛṣṭvā saindhavakaṃ saṃkhye śamam asmāsu dhāsyati
english: 'Will King Duryodhana, on seeing the lord of the Sindhus laid low in battle by Phalguna, make peace with us?'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vinihatān bhrātṝn bhīmasenena saṃyuge kaccid duryodhano mandaḥ śamam asmāsu dhāsyati
english: 'On seeing his brothers slain by Bhīmasena in the fight, will the foolish Duryodhana make peace with us?'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā cānyān bahūn yodhān pātitān dharaṇītale kaccid duryodhano mandaḥ paścāttāpaṃ kariṣyati
english: 'And on seeing many other warriors cast down upon the earth, will the foolish Duryodhana feel remorse?'

sanskrit: kaccid bhīṣmeṇa no vairam ekenaiva praśāmyati śeṣasya rakṣaṇārthaṃ ca saṃdhāsyati suyodhanaḥ
english: 'Shall our enmity be appeased through Bhīṣma alone, and will Suyodhana make a treaty for the protection of those who remain?'

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ tasya cintayānasya pārthiva kṛpayābhiparītasya ghoraṃ yuddham avartata
english: As he pondered thus in many ways, O king, overcome with compassion, the terrible battle raged on.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā tu nardamānaṃ taṃ bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam meghastanitanirghoṣaṃ ke vīrāḥ paryavārayan
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: As the mighty Bhīmasena thus roared with a din like the thunder of clouds, what heroes surrounded him?

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ taṃ vai triṣu lokeṣu saṃjaya kruddhasya bhimasenasya yas tiṣṭhed agrato raṇe
english: For I do not see anyone, Saṃjaya, in the three worlds who could stand before the enraged Bhīmasena in battle.

sanskrit: gadām udyacchamānasya kālasyeva mahāmṛdhe na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ tāta yas tiṣṭheta raṇājire
english: As he lifts his mace in the great fray like Death himself, I do not see, my child, who could stand his ground on the field of battle.

sanskrit: rathaṃ rathena yo hanyāt kuñjaraṃ kuñjareṇa ca kas tasya samare sthātā sākṣād api śatakratuḥ
english: He who would smash a chariot with a chariot and an elephant with an elephant — who could withstand him in battle, even Śatakratu in person?

sanskrit: kruddhasya bhīmasenasya mama putrāñ jighāṃsataḥ duryodhanahite yuktāḥ samatiṣṭhanta ke 'grataḥ
english: When the enraged Bhīmasena sought to slay my sons, who, devoted to Duryodhana's good, stood up before him?

sanskrit: bhīmasenadavāgnes tu mama putratṛṇolapam pradhakṣyato raṇamukhe ke vīrāḥ pramukhe sthitāḥ
english: When the wildfire that is Bhīmasena was about to burn up my sons like grass and reeds at the front of the battle, what heroes stood in his way?

sanskrit: kālyamānān hi me putrān bhīmenāvekṣya saṃyuge kāleneva prajāḥ sarvāḥ ke bhīmaṃ paryavārayan
english: Seeing my sons driven off by Bhīma in the fight, as all creatures are by Time, who surrounded Bhīma?

sanskrit: bhīmavahneḥ pradīptasya mama putrān didhakṣataḥ ke śūrāḥ paryavartanta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: When the blazing fire of Bhīma sought to consume my sons, what brave men turned to face him? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā tu nardamānaṃ taṃ bhīmasenaṃ mahāratham tumulenaiva śabdena karṇo 'py abhyapatad balī
english: Saṃjaya said: As that great chariot-warrior Bhīmasena thus roared, the mighty Karṇa too rushed upon him with a tumultuous shout.

sanskrit: vyākṣipan balavac cāpam atimātram amarṣaṇaḥ karṇas tu yuddham ākāṅkṣan darśayiṣyan balaṃ balī
english: Drawing his powerful bow to its utmost, the impatient and mighty Karṇa, eager for the fight, made ready to display his strength.

sanskrit: prāvepann iva gātrāṇi karṇabhīmasamāgame rathināṃ sādināṃ caiva tayoḥ śrutvā talasvanam
english: At the meeting of Karṇa and Bhīma, the limbs of the chariot-warriors and the horsemen alike trembled, as they heard the clap of the two heroes' palms.

sanskrit: bhīmasenasya ninadaṃ ghoraṃ śrutvā raṇājire khaṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca saṃbaddhāṃ menire kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: Hearing the terrible roar of Bhīmasena on the field of battle, the foremost of warriors fancied that sky and earth had become one.

sanskrit: punar ghoreṇa nādena pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ samare sarvayodhānāṃ dhanūṃṣy abhyapatan kṣitau
english: At another terrible roar of the great-souled son of Pāṇḍu, the bows of all the warriors in the battle fell to the ground.

sanskrit: vitrastāni ca sarvāṇi śakṛnmūtraṃ prasusruvuḥ vāhanāni mahārāja babhūvur vimanāṃsi ca
english: All the beasts of burden, terrified, let flow their dung and urine, O great king, and lost their senses.

sanskrit: prādurāsan nimittāni ghorāṇi ca bahūni ca tasmiṃs tu tumule rājan bhīmakarṇasamāgame
english: Many dreadful portents appeared, O king, at that tumultuous encounter of Bhīma and Karṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇas tu viṃśatyā śarāṇāṃ bhīmam ārdayat vivyādha cāsya tvaritaḥ sūtaṃ pañcabhir āśugaiḥ
english: Then Karṇa wounded Bhīma with a score of arrows, and swiftly pierced his charioteer with five swift shafts.

sanskrit: prahasya bhīmasenas tu karṇaṃ pratyarpayad raṇe sāyakānāṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā kṣiprakārī mahābalaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, laughing, the mighty one quick of hand, repaid Karṇa in the fight with sixty-four arrows.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo maheṣvāsaḥ sāyakāṃś caturo 'kṣipat asaṃprāptāṃs tu tān bhīmaḥ sāyakair nataparvabhiḥ ciccheda bahudhā rājan darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: Karṇa, the great archer, hurled four arrows at him; but Bhīma, before they reached him, cut them to many pieces with his smooth-jointed shafts, O king, displaying the deftness of his hand.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaś chādayām āsa śaravrātair anekaśaḥ saṃchādyamānaḥ karṇena bahudhā pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Karṇa covered him over with multitudes of arrows again and again, and the son of Pāṇḍu was thus enveloped by Karṇa on every side.

sanskrit: ciccheda cāpaṃ karṇasya muṣṭideśe mahārathaḥ vivyādha cainaṃ bahubhiḥ sāyakair nataparvabhiḥ
english: The great chariot-warrior cut Karṇa's bow at the grip, and pierced him with many smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca sūtajaḥ vivyādha samare bhīmaṃ bhīmakarmā mahārathaḥ
english: Then the son of the charioteer, taking up another bow and stringing it, that great chariot-warrior of terrible deeds, pierced Bhīma in the battle.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo bhṛśaṃ kruddhas trīñ śarān nataparvaṇaḥ nicakhānorasi tadā sūtaputrasya vegitaḥ
english: At this Bhīma, exceedingly enraged and impelled with force, then drove three smooth-jointed shafts deep into the breast of the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: taiḥ karṇo 'bhrājata śarair uromadhyagatais tadā mahīdhara ivodagras triśṛṅgo bharatarṣabha
english: With those arrows lodged in the midst of his chest, Karṇa then shone forth, O bull of the Bharatas, like a lofty three-peaked mountain.
